questions.question: Which of the following novels was written by Mulk Raj Anand and focuses on the life of an untouchable?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Untouchable**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The novel **Untouchable**, published in **1935**, is the debut work of **Mulk Raj Anand**, who is considered one of the pioneers of **Indo-Anglian literature**.
 
• The plot depicts a single, grueling day in the life of **Bakha**, a young **outcaste** sweeper and **manual scavenger** who lives in a cantonment town called **Bulashah**.
 
• The narrative focuses on the psychological and social impact of the **caste system** and **social exclusion** in pre-independence India, inspired by the experiences of the author’s own childhood.
 
• The book gained international prominence due to its stark **social realism** and a famous preface written by the English novelist **E.M. Forster**.
 
• The conclusion of the novel presents three possible solutions for the protagonist: **conversion to Christianity**, the **Gandhian path** of spiritual reform, or the introduction of the **flush toilet** to eliminate manual scavenging.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mulk Raj Anand**:

 
 
• A prolific writer and recipient of the **Sahitya Akademi Award** and **Padma Bhushan**.
 
• His other notable works include **Coolie** (1936) and **Two Leaves and a Bud** (1937), both of which deal with the exploitation of the working class.
 
 
 
• **The Guide**:
 
 
• Written by **R.K. Narayan** in **1958**, it centers on **Raju**, a guide in the fictional town of **Malgudi**, and won the **Sahitya Akademi Award**.
 
 
 
• **Train to Pakistan**:
 
 
• A classic novel by **Khushwant Singh** (1956) that narrates the human tragedy and violence during the **1947 Partition** of India.
 
 
 
• **The White Tiger**:
 
 
• Authored by **Aravind Adiga**, this **2008** novel provides a satirical look at Indias class divide and won the **Man Booker Prize**.

questions.question: Under International Hockey Federation (FIH) rules, what is the standard duration of a modern field hockey match?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4 quarters of 15 min**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **International Hockey Federation (FIH)** rules, the standard duration for a modern field hockey match consists of **four quarters** lasting **15 minutes** each.
 
• This format was officially introduced in **September 2014** to enhance the intensity of the game and improve the viewing experience for fans and television audiences.
 
• The transition replaced the previous structure, which consisted of **two halves** of **35 minutes** each, totaling 70 minutes.
 
• The modern **60-minute match** includes specific rest intervals: a **2-minute break** between the first and second quarters, a **2-minute break** between the third and fourth quarters, and a **5-minute half-time** interval between the second and third quarters.
 
• Specific play stoppages are also integrated into the timing; for instance, the clock is stopped for **40 seconds** after a **goal** is scored and after a **penalty corner** is awarded to ensure **maximum active playing time**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Strategic Objectives:**

 
 
• The shift to **15-minute quarters** allows teams to maintain a higher **tempo** and **tactical flexibility**, as coaches have more opportunities to interact with players during the short breaks.
 
• It aligns the sport with other major global team sports that utilize quarter-based systems, such as **basketball** and **American football**.
 
 
 
• **Tie-Breaking Procedures:**
 
 
• In the event of a draw during the knockout stages of major FIH tournaments, modern rules typically dictate a **penalty shootout** (8-second run-ins) rather than **extra time** or **golden goals**.
 
• This ensures that matches adhere to strict **broadcasting schedules** while providing an exciting conclusion for spectators.

questions.question: A deficiency of insulin in the body can lead to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Diabetes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Insulin** is a critical peptide hormone produced and secreted by the **beta cells** of the **islets of Langerhans** located in the **pancreas**.
 
• The primary biological role of **insulin** is to regulate **blood glucose levels** by facilitating the transport of glucose from the bloodstream into the **liver**, **muscle**, and **adipose tissues** for energy use or storage.
 
• A **deficiency of insulin**, whether absolute (as in **Type 1 Diabetes**) or relative (as in **Type 2 Diabetes**), prevents the body from effectively absorbing sugar, leading to **hyperglycemia** (elevated blood sugar).
 
• This metabolic imbalance results in **Diabetes Mellitus**, a chronic condition that can cause complications such as **kidney failure**, **nerve damage**, and **cardiovascular diseases** if left untreated.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Goitre**

 
 
• It is an abnormal enlargement of the **thyroid gland**, often resulting from a lack of **dietary iodine**.
 
• The deficiency affects the production of **thyroxine**, leading the **pituitary gland** to overstimulate the thyroid.
 
 
 
• **Dwarfism**
 
 
• This refers to short stature caused by a **Growth Hormone (GH)** deficiency during childhood.
 
• It is associated with the **anterior pituitary gland**, which fails to secrete enough **somatotropin** for normal bone development.
 
 
 
• **Hypertension**
 
 
• Commonly known as **high blood pressure**, it is a condition where the force of the blood against the **artery walls** is persistently too high.
 
• While it can be linked to **diabetes**, it is primarily driven by factors like **sodium intake**, **stress**, and **obesity**.

questions.question: The banking sector reforms (1991) recommended by the Narasimham Committee included:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**All of these**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Narasimham Committee I** (1991), formally titled the **Committee on the Financial System (CFS)**, was appointed by the **Ministry of Finance** to address the inefficiencies within the Indian banking sector and enhance its **global competitiveness**.
 
• One of the primary recommendations was the adoption of **Capital Adequacy Norms**. The committee suggested that banks should achieve a capital to risk-weighted assets ratio (CRAR) of **8 percent** in alignment with **Bank for International Settlements (BIS)** standards, which later led to the adoption of **Basel-I** norms.
 
• The committee advocated for **Interest Rate Deregulation**, proposing that the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** should cease the administrative fixing of interest rates. This shift allowed market forces to determine rates, fostering a **competitive environment** and improving the **operational efficiency** of commercial banks.
 
• To clean up bank balance sheets, the committee suggested measures for the **Reduction of Non-Performing Assets (NPAs)**. This included the introduction of standardized **Asset Classification** and **Income Recognition** norms, as well as the proposal for an **Asset Reconstruction Fund (ARF)** to take over bad debts at a discount.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other major recommendations of the 1991 committee included:
 
 
• A gradual reduction of the **Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)** from its high levels of 38.5 percent to **25 percent** and a reduction in the **Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)** to increase the availability of funds for **commercial lending**.
 
• Introduction of a **Four-Tier Banking Structure**, comprising international banks, national banks, regional banks, and local banks to improve the systemic organization.
 
• Abolition of **Branch Licensing** policies to provide banks with **functional autonomy** and flexibility in expanding their reach.
 
• Enhanced **Supervisory Control** through the establishment of a quasi-autonomous body under the RBI, which eventually became the **Board for Financial Supervision (BFS)**.

questions.question: What was the primary function of the Ur in Chola administration?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**village-level governance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ur** was a general assembly of the residents in the **Chola administration**, specifically designed to handle **village-level governance** in ordinary settlements.
 
• It primarily consisted of local tax-paying residents and landowners who managed the daily affairs of the village, ensuring smooth **local administration**.
 
• The **Ur** was responsible for the management of **communal resources**, including the maintenance of **irrigation tanks**, village ponds, and grazing lands for cattle.
 
• This body acted as a **judicial and executive authority** at the grass-roots level, resolving land disputes and collecting local dues to be passed to the state.
 
• The existence of the **Ur** signifies the highly **decentralized** nature of the **Chola Empire**, where local assemblies enjoyed significant autonomy in decision-making.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other Local Assemblies**:

 
 
• **Sabha or Mahasabha**: This was an assembly of **Brahmin** adult males found in **Brahmadeya** villages (lands gifted to Brahmins). It operated through specialized committees called **Variyams**.
 
• **Nagaram**: This was an organization of **merchants** and traders found in commercial towns and trade centers, managing market-related activities and urban **taxation**.
 
 
 
• **Administrative Structure**:
 
 
• The **Chola Empire** was structured into **Mandalams** (provinces), which were further divided into **Valanadus** and **Nadus** (districts).
 
• The **Uttaramerur Inscriptions**, dating to the reign of **Parantaka I**, provide comprehensive details about the eligibility criteria and the **Kudavolai** (lot) system used to elect members to these local bodies.

questions.question: "Stagflation" is a situation of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Inflation + Unemployment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Stagflation** is a unique economic condition characterized by a combination of **stagnant economic growth**, **high unemployment**, and **high inflation** occurring simultaneously.
 
• The term is a portmanteau of **stagnation** and **inflation**, famously coined by British politician **Iain Macleod** during a speech to the House of Commons in **1965**.
 
• It represents a contradiction in traditional **Keynesian economics**, which suggests that inflation and unemployment usually have an inverse relationship, as described by the **Phillips Curve**.
 
• In a stagflationary environment, the **purchasing power** of consumers erodes due to rising prices, while the **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** remains flat or declines, leading to widespread job losses.
 
• This situation creates a **policy dilemma** for central banks, as standard measures to curb inflation (like raising **interest rates**) typically exacerbate unemployment, while measures to boost employment can further fuel inflation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Primary Causes of Stagflation:**

 
 
• **Supply Shocks:** Sudden constraints in the supply of essential commodities, such as the **1973 Oil Crisis**, which led to a spike in **energy costs** and production expenses globally.
 
• **Monetary Mismanagement:** Excessive expansion of the **money supply** by a central bank while the economy is facing production bottlenecks.
 
• **Structural Rigidities:** Inefficiencies in the **labor market** or excessive government regulations that prevent the economy from adjusting to supply-side changes.
 
 
 
• **Economic Indicators:**
 
 
• **Misery Index:** This index is calculated by adding the **unemployment rate** to the **inflation rate**, and it reaches peak levels during periods of stagflation.
 
• **Cost-Push Inflation:** Unlike demand-pull inflation, stagflation is often driven by **rising input costs** (wages, raw materials) rather than excessive consumer demand.

questions.question: Loo is ____ and ____ local wind of northern plane of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**hot, dry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Loo** is a powerful, gusty, and intense **local wind** that specifically characterizes the summer climate of the **Northern Plains** (Indo-Gangetic Plain) of India and Pakistan.
 
• It is scientifically classified as a **hot and dry** wind, usually blowing during the peak summer months of **May** and **June** when the thermal gradient is highest.
 
• These winds typically originate from the **Thar Desert** in Rajasthan and the arid regions of **Balochistan**, gaining heat as they travel across the sun-scorched plains.
 
• The temperature of the Loo often ranges between **45°C** and **50°C**, which is significantly higher than the average ambient temperature, leading to extreme **heatwaves**.
 
• The **dryness** of the Loo is a result of the wind passing over vast landmasses with minimal moisture, causing rapid **evaporation** and severe **thermal discomfort** for all living organisms.
 
• Direct exposure to this wind is extremely dangerous and can lead to fatal **heatstrokes** or **hyperthermia** due to the body's inability to cool down through sweating in such parched conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Classification of Local Winds**:

 
 
• **Chinook**: Known as the **Snow Eater**, these are warm, dry winds that descend the eastern slopes of the **Rocky Mountains** in North America.
 
• **Mistral**: A **cold and dry** wind that blows from the north through the Rhone Valley toward the **Mediterranean Sea** during winter.
 
• **Harmattan**: A dry, dusty wind blowing from the **Sahara Desert** toward the West African coast, known locally as **The Doctor** for its cooling effect on humid air.
 
• **Sirocco**: A **Mediterranean wind** that comes from the Sahara and reaches hurricane speeds in North Africa and Southern Europe as a hot, dry wind.
 
 
 
• **Related Indian Phenomena**:
 
 
• **Mango Showers**: Pre-monsoon rainfall in **Karnataka** and **Kerala** that assists in the ripening of mangoes and provides relief from the summer heat.
 
• **Kal Baisakhi**: Violent thunderstorms or **Nor'westers** that occur in **West Bengal** and **Assam**, bringing localized rain and cooling.
 
• **Elephantine**: A local wind in the **Malabar Coast** that marks the transition towards the end of the monsoon season.

questions.question: The next census of India will be conducted in how many phases?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The upcoming **Census of India** is scheduled to be conducted in **two distinct phases** to ensure systematic data collection across the vast geography of the country.
 
• **Phase I** is the **Houselisting and Housing Census**. During this phase, enumerators visit every house to record data concerning the **structure of the house**, available **amenities** (like water and electricity), and assets owned by the household.
 
• **Phase II** is the **Population Enumeration**. This is the stage where the actual headcounting of the population takes place, collecting detailed information on **demographics**, **religion**, **literacy**, **occupation**, and **migration**.
 
• The next census will be the first **Digital Census** in India, where data will be collected through a **mobile application** instead of traditional paper forms, allowing for faster processing and analysis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Administrative Framework**:

 
 
• The census is conducted under the **Census Act, 1948**.
 
• The nodal agency is the **Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner**, which operates under the **Ministry of Home Affairs**.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context**:
 
 
• The first non-synchronous census in India was held in **1872** during the tenure of **Lord Mayo**.
 
• The first **synchronous census** (conducted simultaneously across the country) took place in **1881** under **Lord Ripon**.
 
• Since 1881, the census has been conducted every **10 years** without fail until the 2021 cycle was delayed.
 
 
 
• **Significance**:
 
 
• Census data is vital for **delimitation of constituencies**, **resource allocation**, and framing government welfare policies.

questions.question: On 9th May 2025, who held that it is not the duty of courts to instruct the media to delete or take down content?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Supreme Court of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On **9th May 2025**, the **Supreme Court of India** emphasized that the **judiciary** should not assume the role of an **editorial board** or a content regulator for the media.
 
• The bench clarified that it is not the **inherent duty** of the courts to issue orders for the **deletion** or **takedown** of published news content, as this falls under **editorial autonomy**.
 
• This observation reinforces the **Freedom of Speech and Expression** guaranteed under **Article 19(1)(a)** of the **Constitution of India**, protecting the press from **judicial censorship**.
 
• The court highlighted that **judicial intervention** in removing content should only occur when there is a clear violation of **statutory laws**, **public order**, or **national security**.
 
• This ruling promotes **judicial restraint** and maintains the **separation of powers** by preventing courts from overstepping into the domain of **media regulation** and content management.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Supreme Court of India**:

 
 
• It is the **highest judicial authority** in India, established on **28th January 1950**.
 
• The court exercises **Original, Appellate, and Advisory jurisdiction** and is the final interpreter of the **Constitution**.
 
 
 
• **Allahabad High Court**:
 
 
• Established in **1866**, it is one of the oldest **High Courts** in India and has the highest number of **sanctioned judges**.
 
 
 
• **Law Commission of India**:
 
 
• An **advisory body** that works for **legal reform** and is typically composed of legal experts and headed by a retired judge.
 
 
 
• **Patna High Court**:
 
 
• The High Court for the state of **Bihar**, established in **1916** under the **Letters Patent**.
 
 
 
• **Article 19(1)(a)**:
 
 
• Ensures **Freedom of Speech and Expression**, which includes **freedom of the press**, subject to **reasonable restrictions** under **Article 19(2)**.

questions.question:
According to the Indian Constitution, which of the following pair of subject – list is correct?

I. Adoption and Succession – State list

II. Trade and Commerce – Concurrent List
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Neither I nor II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Seventh Schedule** of the **Indian Constitution**, under **Article 246**, distributes legislative powers between the Union and the States through the **Union List**, **State List**, and **Concurrent List**.
 
• **Adoption and Succession**: These subjects are explicitly mentioned under **Entry 5** of the **Concurrent List** (List III), which includes marriage, divorce, infants, minors, adoption, and all matters related to **succession** and **wills**. Hence, statement I is incorrect.
 
• **Trade and Commerce**: **Entry 26** of the **State List** (List II) deals with trade and commerce within the state, while **Entry 42** of the **Union List** (List I) covers inter-state trade and commerce; these are not classified as general subjects of the **Concurrent List**. Hence, statement II is incorrect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Union List (List I)**:

 
 
• Includes subjects of national importance such as **Defense**, **Foreign Affairs**, **Atomic Energy**, **Banking**, and **Post and Telegraph**.
 
• The **Parliament** has the exclusive power to legislate on the 100 items currently listed.
 
 
 
• **State List (List II)**:
 
 
• Includes subjects related to local interest such as **Public Order**, **Police**, **Public Health**, **Sanitation**, and **Agriculture**.
 
• The **State Legislature** typically has exclusive authority over these 61 items.
 
 
 
• **Concurrent List (List III)**:
 
 
• Features 52 items where both the **Central Government** and **State Governments** share jurisdiction.
 
• Examples include **Education**, **Forests**, **Criminal Law**, **Protection of Wild Animals and Birds**, and **Trade Unions**.
 
• In case of a conflict between Union and State laws on these subjects, the **Union Law** prevails.

questions.question: What is the lift off weight of ISRO's Small Satellite Launch Vehicle (SSLV)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**120 tonnes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Small Satellite Launch Vehicle (SSLV)** is a small-lift launch vehicle developed by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** to deliver satellites into **Low Earth Orbit (LEO)**.
 
• The vehicle features a **lift-off weight** of approximately **120 tonnes**, making it a much lighter and more compact rocket compared to the **Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV)** which weighs around **320 tonnes**.
 
• It stands at a **height of 34 meters** with a **diameter of 2 meters**, designed for high flexibility and efficiency in launch operations.
 
• The **SSLV** is specifically engineered for **launch-on-demand** capability, allowing for a **turnaround time** of just **72 hours** and requiring only **6 people** for integration.
 
• It is capable of carrying a payload mass of up to **500 kg** to a **500 km planar orbit**, making it ideal for the commercial **small satellite market**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Technical Specifications and Architecture:
 
 
• **Propulsion System**: The vehicle is a **three-stage** rocket where all the primary stages utilize **solid propulsion** technology for simplified logistics and lower costs.
 
• **Velocity Trimming Module (VTM)**: It features a liquid-based terminal stage that ensures precise **orbital injection** and **velocity trimming** for the payloads.
 
• **Mission Capability**: The **SSLV** can accommodate multiple satellite deployments, including **nanosatellites**, **microsatellites**, and **mini-satellites**.
 
• **Strategic Goal**: By reducing the cost of access to space, **ISRO** aims to capture a significant share of the global small satellite launch market through its commercial arm, **NewSpace India Limited (NSIL)**.
 
• **Historical Milestones**: The successful **SSLV-D2** mission in **February 2023** demonstrated the vehicle's capability by placing the **EOS-07**, **Janus-1**, and **AzaadiSAT-2** satellites into their intended orbits.

questions.question: Why are the soles of shoes grooved?

options.text: To provide better grip and safety
To reduce the weight of shoes

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To provide better grip and safety**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary scientific reason for grooving shoe soles is to increase the **frictional force** between the shoe and the ground surface.
 
• By creating deep patterns and **roughness** on the sole, the surface area for **mechanical interlocking** increases, which prevents the foot from sliding forward or backward during movement.
 
• In the presence of **lubricants** like water, oil, or mud, these grooves act as **drainage channels** to expel the liquid, ensuring that the rubber material maintains direct contact with the solid ground.
 
• Increased **traction** provided by grooved soles is a critical safety requirement for **locomotion**, as it allows the body to apply a **reaction force** against the ground to move without falling.
 
• This design is essential for preventing **accidental slips** and injuries, especially on smooth, wet, or uneven surfaces where the **coefficient of friction** is naturally low.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Frictional Physics**:

 
 
• **Static Friction**: The grooves help maintain a high level of **static friction**, which is the force that keeps an object at rest when a force is applied.
 
• **Kinetic Friction**: Once in motion, the **tread pattern** ensures that kinetic friction remains high enough to control stopping distances and direction changes.
 
 
 
• **Specialized Tread Patterns**:
 
 
• **Herringbone Pattern**: Commonly used in **basketball shoes** to provide maximum grip for quick **pivoting** and lateral movements on hardwood courts.
 
• **Lugged Soles**: Found in **hiking boots**, these utilize deep, wide grooves to provide stability on loose soil, rocks, and **rugged terrain**.
 
• **Cleats**: In sports like **football** or **soccer**, the grooves are replaced by large protrusions (studs) to penetrate soft surfaces for extreme grip.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Application**:
 
 
• **Safety Footwear** in factories often follows specific **ISO standards** for slip resistance, requiring specialized grooving to handle spills of industrial chemicals or grease.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Tires**:
 
 
• Much like shoes, **automobile tires** utilize a similar concept called **tread**. A bald tire (one without grooves) is prone to **hydroplaning**, where a layer of water builds up between the tire and the road, leading to a complete loss of control.
